catalog_quote: (p.26) Stress is predictable, generally falling on the ultimate or penultimate syllable. ... (p.27) 2.1 Stress. As mentioned above, stress is predictable in the language, and generally falls on the penultimate syllable as seen in (5). 5) ... [ka.'pu.la] 'egg' ... [pa.ta.ra.'wɔ.ŋa] 'sacrifice' When suffixes are added to the root word, the stress will shift and remain on the penultimate syllable. ... There are exceptions to this general rule when considering vowel glides and reduplication, but in both cases the exceptions are also predictable. When a word ends in a diphthong, that is, CVV̯, the stress falls on the final syllable of the word, as shown on (9). 9) [ŋa.'laj] 'large' [ᵐbʷa.ta.'qɔj] 'sore' [ᵐbau̯] 'hand' [nɔ.'nɔu̯] 'enmity' When suffixes are added to words ending in the CVV̯ pattern, the stress once again falls on the penultimate syllable, as shown in (10). (2) Deciding source is a dedicated 46-pp phonology article (1993) by the resident SIL linguist -- the only phonology in Glottolog's bibliography and the best available description; the only other descriptive work (Clark & Clark 1987 grammar sketch) is also held and agrees (plain penultimate stress under a (C)V-only syllable analysis, which is extensionally the 1993 rule 'penult, but final if the word ends in CVV̯'). (3) No works still to obtain: Glottolog 5.1 lists nothing descriptive beyond the two held works
